To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a synchronously pumped optical parametric oscillator with a resonant nonlinearity was realized in sodium vapor and its parameters were studied as a function of the sodium concentration and the resonator length.
we have investigated the parametric generation of light with picosecond pulses in sodium vapor in the resonator pumped synchronously by picosecond pulses.
a resonant optical four-photon parametric oscillator based upon the nonlinear optical response of sodium vapor has been demonstrated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of nonlinear optical effects in sodium vapor and their applications in optical parametric oscillators.
the development of new nonlinear-optical methods of generating coherent radiation in a wide spectral range.
the development of new methods for the generation of tunable radiation based on nonlinear optical effects in gases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present study has provided an experimental basis for the use of a sodium optical parametric amplifier for the amplification of short pulses of coherent radiation in the visible and near-infrared regions of the spectrum.

a four-photon parametric oscillator based in sodium vapor has been demonstrated and the dependence of the main characteristics of the output radiation on the sodium concentration, optical resonator length, and pump intensity has been investigated.
a four-photon parametric oscillator with sodium vapor as the nonlinear medium has been developed and investigated in detail.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a four-wave parametric oscillator can be realized in a synchronously bichromatically pumped resonator.

a new type of parametric oscillator has been demonstrated which is based on a resonant third-order nonlinear process and which is characterized by high conversion efficiency and good spectral quality of the output radiation.
the resonator is an effective tool for the generation of coherent radiation in a medium with a resonant nonlinearity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optical parametric oscillation is a very efficient process.
the optical parametric oscillator with resonant third-order nonlinearities is an effective source of tunable picosecond radiation.
the resonator geometry is very important for obtaining the maximum efficiency of the parametric oscillator.
